Beat It On Down the Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dancin' in the Streets** (2 reviews): Reviewer and friend then preferred Van Halen's version of Dancing in the Street to the Dead's [36][37]
- **Loser** (1 review): Enjoys the first-set country-western stretch running from C.C. Rider into Loser, then Mama Tried through Beat It On Down the Line [30]
- **Beat It On Down the Line** (1 review): Says Beat It On Down the Line shreds [32]
- **Deal** (1 review): Says Deal shreds [32]
- **Touch of Grey** (1 review): An anniversary banner dropped at the end of a rousing Touch of Grey [33]
- **Samson and Delilah** (1 review): Stage and house lights faded to a reddish haze, with a long percussion-led intro into Samson [33]
- **High Time** (1 review): Calls the High Time among the greatest the reviewer has heard [38]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Likes Let It Grow being placed before Drums, in old-school fashion [38]

## The recordings

- **gd85-11-07.sbd.connor.5300.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 142 min; rated 4.38/5 by 13 [1]
- **gd1985-11-07.148632.fob.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 21 songs; 139 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1985-11-07.151999.senn441.lamarre.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 132 min [6]
- **gd1985-11-07.schoeps.oade.22798.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 20 songs; 138 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [11]. Said about its sound: The PCM master has two seconds of digital noise at the start of disc one, track two [11]

## Around the show

- The reviewer attended wearing a full-length leg cast, which they remembered as very odd [28]
- Describes the Rochester crowd as one of the most high-energy on the East Coast [30]
- Remembers gooney birds all over the place at the show [31]
- Confirms a banner was unfurled, though the reviewer has seen no photo of it [32]
- Mentions the old rink venue was refurbished some years back [34]
- Recalls gooney birds, and made t-shirts of them with a photo from the show [35]
- Remembers Bob sitting on stage playing slide in front of them, unsure which night [35]
- This was the reviewer's first Dead show; they knew few songs beforehand [36]
- Calls this and the other Rochester show both solid by 1985 standards [28]
- Judges the show solid rather than especially tremendous [36]
- Judges the show solid rather than especially tremendous [37]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd85-11-07.sbd.connor.5300.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD (MSC> Reel> DAT> CDR> TAE> CDR> EAC> Shnv3) with AUD patches (FOB AUD> Beyer Dynamic M88's>Sony TCD5M(CM)>Nak DR-10 (Playback)> Midiman Flying Cow… [1]
- **gd1985-11-07.148632.fob.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Michael Hessberg; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Michael Hessberg's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser ME-80 mics > Sony D5M [2]. Also: A Schoeps CMC4 MK41 source supplies a 4-second patch in Cumberland Blues and a 13-second one in Space [2]
- **gd1985-11-07.151999.senn441.lamarre.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Recorded by Doug Lamarre; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Doug Lamarre's Master Audience Cassettes (Taper's Section); Sennheiser 441 mics > Sony D5M [6]. Also: A Sennheiser ME80 source supplies early crowd and Beat It On Down the Line, plus a 26-second Drums to Space patch [6]
- **gd1985-11-07.schoeps.oade.22798.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Oade Brothers; transferred by dwonk; source: Schoeps CMC441 (TS, 90deg, 17cm) > Oade M118 > Oade modSONY PCM-F1 [11]

claims.text: The reviewer attended wearing a full-length leg cast, which they remembered as very odd
Calls this and the other Rochester show both solid by 1985 standards
Describes the Rochester crowd as one of the most high-energy on the East Coast
Enjoys the first-set country-western stretch running from C.C. Rider into Loser, then Mama Tried through Beat It On Down the Line
Says Stella Blue stumbles in places
Remembers gooney birds all over the place at the show
Confirms a banner was unfurled, though the reviewer has seen no photo of it

claims.text: Says Beat It On Down the Line shreds
Says Deal shreds
An anniversary banner dropped at the end of a rousing Touch of Grey
Stage and house lights faded to a reddish haze, with a long percussion-led intro into Samson
Mentions the old rink venue was refurbished some years back
Recalls gooney birds, and made t-shirts of them with a photo from the show
Remembers Bob sitting on stage playing slide in front of them, unsure which night
This was the reviewer's first Dead show; they knew few songs beforehand
Reviewer and friend then preferred Van Halen's version of Dancing in the Street to the Dead's
Judges the show solid rather than especially tremendous

Judges the show solid rather than especially tremendous
Calls the High Time among the greatest the reviewer has heard
Likes Let It Grow being placed before Drums, in old-school fashion
Audience patches came from front-of-board Beyer M88 mics into a Sony TCD5M, played back via Nak DR-10
Master cassette from Michael Hessberg, front-of-board Sennheiser ME80; Charlie Miller did the transfer and coordination
A Schoeps CMC4 MK41 source supplies a 4-second patch in Cumberland Blues and a 13-second one in Space
Master cassettes from Doug Lamarre on Sennheiser 441 mics; Charlie Miller transferred and coordinated
A Sennheiser ME80 source supplies early crowd and Beat It On Down the Line, plus a 26-second Drums to Space patch
The PCM master has two seconds of digital noise at the start of disc one, track two
